title: Gemini Ecosystem and Interfaces
summary: This intermediate-level module enables learners to distinguish an interactive browser workspace from programmatic access to Gemini. After completing it, learners can select an interface that fits experimentation or application integration and explain the resulting workflow.
objectives: Distinguish the role of Google AI Studio from the role of the Gemini API.
Choose an appropriate Gemini interface for interactive experimentation or application integration.
Describe the basic boundary between an application and the Gemini API without relying on model-specific details.
Explain what changed in this source-currency update and what instructional material it affected.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes familiarity with writing prompts and with the basic idea that an application can send a request to an external service and receive a response. No catalogue prerequisite is required, and the module explains the relevant interface choices without assuming knowledge of a particular programming language, model, software library, or configuration key.
In this module, an interface means the point through which a person or an application interacts with Gemini. The interface choice changes how work is tested, integrated, and operated.

sections.title: Interactive experimentation
paragraphs: Google AI Studio is a browser-based environment for experimenting with Gemini. A learner can use it to try instructions and inputs interactively, inspect results, and refine a prompt before deciding how an application should use it.

This interface is appropriate when the immediate task is exploration. It reduces the need to build an application before testing whether an instruction and its context produce useful results. An interactive result is still evidence from a test, not a guarantee that an integrated application will behave identically under every input.

sections.title: Programmatic access
paragraphs: The Gemini API is the programmatic interface. An application sends input in a request and receives a response that the application can process. This boundary lets developers place Gemini within a larger workflow, such as accepting user input, applying application logic, handling a response, and presenting or storing an output.

Programmatic integration adds responsibilities that an isolated interactive test does not settle. The application must determine what input to send, how to handle unsuccessful requests or unsuitable responses, and how the returned material may be used. Specific model choices, software libraries, credential procedures, limits, and configuration details are intentionally omitted because they are not established by the supplied material for this correction.

sections.title: Choosing an interface
paragraphs: Choose Google AI Studio when the main goal is to explore prompts and inspect results interactively. Choose the Gemini API when software must send requests and use responses as part of an application workflow.

These interfaces can support different stages of one workflow. Interactive experimentation can help clarify the desired behavior, while programmatic access can place that behavior inside an application. Moving from experimentation to integration requires testing in the application context because application inputs, error handling, and output use are part of the integrated system.
sections.callout: Interface selection is a workflow decision. Interactive experimentation supports exploration, while the Gemini API supports application integration.

sections.title: Source currency update
paragraphs: The previous cited source was the local path content/modules/google-gemini-practice/gemini-ecosystem-and-interfaces.json. It was identified as an unregistered publisher source that had never been verified. This update replaces that citation with official Google documentation available over HTTPS.

The source change affects the module's attribution, verification date, and support for the distinction between Google AI Studio and the Gemini API. The correction does not add model names, version numbers, software library names, configuration keys, limits, or other details not established for this update.

questions.prompt: Which interface should a learner choose when the immediate goal is to experiment with prompts interactively before building an application?
questions.explanation: The module identifies Google AI Studio as the browser-based environment for interactive prompt experimentation.

questions.prompt: Which interface is intended for software that must send input and process a returned response as part of an application workflow?
questions.explanation: The Gemini API is the programmatic interface used by an application to send requests and process responses.

questions.prompt: What did this currency update change?
choices: It replaced an unverified local citation with official Google documentation and updated the source-verification basis.
It introduced specific model versions and configuration keys.
It changed the module from intermediate to advanced.
questions.explanation: The currency-update section says the unverified local citation was replaced by official Google documentation. It also says that model versions and configuration keys were not added.
